It maintains continuous local programming by managing <cite id="4">the AUCC Food Pantry (Ummah's Kitchen) alongside youth and recreation programs</cite>. rich_narrative.summary: Al Ummah Community Center operates a local food pantry and fitness facility built on Islamic principles of public service in New Jersey <cite id="4">through Ummah's Kitchen and gym programs</cite>. However, significant financial and efficiency constraints limit its current overall operations. In FY2025, the organization recorded <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $334,780</cite>, marking a notable revenue drop from prior years. The organization directs a <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 42.9%</cite> to its direct activities, leaving over half of its budget allocated to administrative and operational overhead. This program spending level remains significantly below the <cite id="1">75% industry standard benchmark</cite> and the <cite id="1">83.5% peer program ratio median</cite>. Financially, annual expenses exceed incoming revenue, requiring drawn-down reserves to sustain short-term operations, even though the center holds <cite id="1">9.0 months of working capital</cite>. External rating agencies like Charity Navigator give the center <cite id="1">an overall score of 71/100</cite>. While the center maintains active community-level services, structural financial deficits and limited outcome measurement present persistent challenges to its sustainability.
